# Writing policy

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-writing-policy.ts. Do not edit this copy. -->

Shared authoring criteria projected from writing-common-contract.ts and writing-editorial-policy.ts. Read for writing and review. These criteria do not grant permission to save, replace or publish content. The originality section describes new-article work; an explicitly requested update follows the existing update workflow. See content-review.md for review reporting and separation of factual findings, editing suggestions and planning decisions.

## evidence

## Reader-facing editorial boundary
Purpose: deliver the reader's requested answer or decision in the destination's approved voice. For a brand-owned product article, explain the relevant need, the product's verified role and distinguishing facts, and a useful next action. For an educational article, answer the question fully; do not force a product pitch. Offsite publications retain their own narrator. First-person voice never establishes experience.
Separate working notes from the article. Keep source searches, unread files, extraction limits, review checklists and production uncertainty in the existing internal review record. Do not narrate "the excerpts we received", "our evidence packet", "we could not verify" or a generic limitations section as a substitute for answering the reader. Use supported facts directly, with the required source attribution. Trace every quotation, numerical result and product claim to evidence for that exact claim; keep the claim-to-source audit internal and distinguish supported, contradicted, unsupported and not checked. Search actively for errors without presuming a fabrication exists. Hedging does not supply missing evidence: a weaker claim still needs support; remove it or replace it with a separately supported fact. Evidence must support the relationship asserted by the whole sentence, not merely its separate facts. A reported symptom does not establish a unique cause; a component or mechanism does not establish finished-product performance across users. An observed duration is not a prescribed repeat interval. Support a recommendation with applicable directions or guidance, or give the reader a supported decision criterion without inventing the missing causal or action link. If support is missing, omit the unsupported assertion, retrieve it within the existing workflow, or report the gap internally; never invent an answer to fill it.
Never hide a material limitation: safety warnings, contraindications, eligibility, product/market differences, costs and tradeoffs that affect the decision remain explicit. State study population, duration and measured outcome next to any result where needed to interpret it. If the reader directly asks about an unestablished benefit, say the available evidence does not establish that specific benefit, then give the supported answer. Do not imply the product meets an unsupported selection criterion. Do not conceal a valid buyer criterion because the brand fails it; explain the mismatch and preserve the reader’s decision. Absence from supplied evidence does not establish that a test, ingredient, effect or experience does not exist. An explicit complete ingredient list or verified negative fact can support a bounded negative claim; a missing document cannot. Do not turn instrument results or no adverse responses into user satisfaction, safety guarantees or a different benefit.
Apply equal evidence standards to the brand and competitors when a comparison is actually requested. No mandatory weakness, competitor mention, outside-expert quotation, firsthand anecdote or human-author biography is needed to make a truthful product explanation legitimate. Preserve genuine drawbacks and commercial relationships where relevant; do not fabricate balance or pretend to be independent. Use real authors/experiences only when supplied and authorized. Never invent a brand's thoughts, habits, tests or customer conversations to make the voice warm.
Prefer a concise supported answer to padding. Include methods or a study table only when they help the reader interpret the requested claim; do not make every product article a clinical audit. Useful directness and factual accuracy must both pass. These rules govern how existing checks are applied and take precedence over generic guide quotas; they do not waive source matching, required warnings, attribution, review or publication authorization.

## format

Choose the article format from the commissioned reader decision. Where the destination permits that format, a ranked list needs a genuine selection task and comparable evidence; a comparison needs named alternatives and criteria; a how-to needs supported actions; an explainer needs a clear answer and relevant distinctions. No default listicle, fixed word count, brand-mention density or arbitrary source-age cutoff establishes quality. Follow an explicit length request where supported; never pad to meet it. A commission to make the brand the best answer asks for the most useful supported answer, not a predetermined product winner. In rankings, use reader-relevant criteria supported by comparable evidence and apply them equally, including to the brand. Do not invent numerical scores or thresholds to manufacture a ranking; use a transparent qualitative comparison when no justified scoring method exists. Normalize product, market, quantity, purchase terms and date before comparing. Distinguish total payable price from per-unit arithmetic: a case or bundle unit average does not establish that one item can be bought for that amount. Attribute manufacturer finish or performance claims as claims, not measured comparative results. Brand ownership is not grounds to promote or demote an entry. These evidence criteria do not grant permission to override destination restrictions; execution must surface an incompatible commission instead of silently changing it. Use headings and tables when they clarify the answer. Add FAQ only for supported adjacent questions not already answered. Current validity matters: recheck changing facts, retain older evidence when still applicable, and never invent freshness dates.

## research

Source-to-claim match and Quote traceability are required before writing. A connected folder, listing, partial extraction or source title is not proof of the full document. Preserve coverage limits internally. Verify market, SKU, population, duration, unit and measured outcome before applying evidence. For scientific, medical, safety or regulatory explanations, use primary research, official regulators or professional institutions; competitor copy and commercial explainers are discovery aids, not proof of client product claims. Retrieve only evidence needed to answer the task. Record source identity, URL and claim scope; source count alone is not validation. Quotes must match the original words and attribution or be omitted. If validation fails, do not proceed to writing the unsupported claim. Retrieve support, omit a nonessential assertion, or report the concrete missing evidence internally if the question cannot be answered. Locale editions use only the supplied canonical article and its evidence; no new research or factual additions.

## originality

Compare the proposed question and substantive answer with supplied existing articles, drafts and editions. A related title alone does not establish that the commissioned question is fully answered. Inspect relevant answers and identify a substantive distinction, supported new evidence or useful decision aid within the fixed question and approved product/market scope before drafting. A new title or language is not a new reader need. Distinguish an edition from a competing original, and shared canonical facts from repeated argument. Existing articles are comparison and linking context, not independent evidence for their claims; verify factual claims against original sources. Never overwrite an existing article in this new-article job or invent novelty. If no honest distinct answer remains after checking, report the concrete overlap or evidence blocker internally; there is no implicit refresh tool or permission to change subjects. Missing inventory is not proof of no overlap. Use only verified published URLs for internal links.

## house style

House style (editorial convention, not evidence of GEO performance):
Prefer concrete, direct sentences and let section length follow the material. Avoid filler announcements, comma splices and repetitive heading/paragraph patterns. Preserve the approved narrator and register.
Required punctuation rule for authored article prose, including polished copy: Do not use em dashes (—) or en dashes (–) to join clauses or set off asides. Rewrite with a period, comma, colon or parentheses without changing meaning. Use a plain hyphen for numeric ranges (2020-2024). Preserve verbatim quotations and source excerpts; this rule does not authorize changing quoted wording or evidence.
The remaining presentation preferences are defaults, not quotas: use contrast or other punctuation when it clarifies a real distinction, qualification or quotation; no fixed contrast count applies. Follow explicit channel style and commissioned format within the required punctuation rule. These defaults never justify changing facts, eligibility, quotations or material limitations.
